records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Introduction to Vines and Wines
records.description: The importance of viticulture (grape growing) and enology (winemaking); wine quality.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Grapevine Physiology
records.description: Botanical and physiological concepts related to grapevine growth and development including photosynthesis, water relations, mineral nutrient impacts, and grapevine response to environmental conditions.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Viticulture I
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: BIOLOGY 106 or 120; SOIL SCI 201; VIT ENOL 113; VIT ENOL 280.
records.description: Fall viticulture theory and practices including identification and utilization of rootstocks, wine grapes, and wild species; grape species taxonomy and diversity; breeding efforts for grapevine improvement and clean plant material.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Viticulture I Laboratory
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: Concurrent enrollment in VIT ENOL 311.
records.description: Fall viticulture theory and practices laboratory focused on identification of wine grapes, rootstocks, and wild species; grape species taxonomy and diversity, harvest decisions and practices.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Wine Fermentation and Production
records.description: Principles and practices of wine fermentation and production.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Wine Fermentation and Production Laboratory
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: Concurrent enrollment in VIT ENOL 322.
records.description: Hands-on experience with the production of still and sparkling wine; evaluation of the impacts of vineyard practices, environment, cultivar, vintage, and production methods on wine composition and quality with a winemaking project. Must be 18 years of age or older to participate.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Winery Operations and Equipment
records.description: Fundamentals and practices for the unit operations and equipment involved in wine production from fruit receiving through bottling.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Winery Operations and Equipment Laboratory Field Trip
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: By department permission; concurrent enrollment in VIT ENOL 340.
records.description: Week-long field trip over Spring Break to visit wineries and wine industry suppliers, specific visits vary by year but will include several wineries, at least one cooperage, and several equipment and packaging suppliers.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Special Topics in Viticulture and Enology
records.description: Assessment and evaluation of special topics in viticulture and enology. Credit not granted for both VIT ENOL 401 and 501.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Viticulture II
records.description: Winter and spring viticulture theory and practices including water relations and irrigation, major pest pressures, training and trellising, pruning, berry composition, light, and temperature.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Viticulture II Laboratory
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: Concurrent enrollment in VIT ENOL 414.
records.description: Winter and spring viticulture theory and practices laboratory focused on pruning, trellising, and training; addressing vineyard nutrient issues; sprayer calibration; and assessing vine water status.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Wine Sensory
records.description: Introduction to theory, principles, and applications of sensory evaluation techniques for the evaluation of appearance, aroma, flavor and texture of foods and wine; basic psychological and physiological processes underlying sensory analysis, sensory testing methodologies and the basic principles of flavor perception and chemistry.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Wine Sensory Laboratory
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: VIT ENOL 422 or concurrent enrollment.
records.description: Principles and application of sensory evaluation techniques for the evaluation of the appearance, aroma, flavor, and texture of wine. Typically offered Spring.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Wine Chemistry
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MBIOS 101 or 305; MBIOS 303 or CHEM 370; concurrent enrollment in BIOLOGY 420.
records.description: Study of the chemistry and biochemistry of fruits; biochemistry and physiology of individual fruit compounds, aspects of processing including winemaking. Credit not granted for both VIT ENOL 438 and 538.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Wine Chemistry Laboratory
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: Concurrent enrollment in VIT ENOL 438.
records.description: Assay wine and juice for its chemical constituents; laboratory safety in a wine chemistry setting. Credit not granted for both VIT ENOL 439 and 539.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Micro and Molecular Biology of Wine
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MBIOS 101 or 305; MBIOS 303 or CHEM 370; VIT ENOL 322.
records.description: Molecular and microbiological aspects of yeast, filamentous fungi, and lactic acid bacteria fermentation of grape juice or must to produce still, sparkling, and aged wine; production and preservation of microbial starter cultures and the application of hazard analysis and critical control point systems; assessment of normal, stuck, and sluggish fermentations. Credit not granted for both VIT ENOL 482 and 582.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Micro and Molecular Biology of Wine Laboratory
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: Concurrent enrollment in VIT ENOL 482.
records.description: Identification of microorganisms (non-spoilage and spoilage) using microscopic, molecular, and selective media methods; evaluation of factors related to the survival of yeast and bacteria in wine; strategies for restarting stuck yeast and malolactic fermentations. Credit not granted for both VIT ENOL 483 and 583.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Seminar in Viticulture and Enology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: VIT ENOL 113; VIT ENOL 280.
records.description: Current topics in viticulture and enology; designed to enhance student educational pathways and career goals.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Critical Thinking in Vineyard and Winery Management
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: VIT ENOL 311; VIT ENOL 340; VIT ENOL 414.
records.description: Integration and application of knowledge of grape production and wine science to major issues of the industry; improvement planning for existing winery and vineyard operations; incorporation of the principles of economic and environmental sustainability; leadership skill development applicable to the grape and wine industry.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Undergraduate Research in Viticulture and Enology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: By instructor permission; admitted to the major in Viticulture and Enology; junior standing.
records.description: Research in viticulture and enology under faculty guidance.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: VIT_ENOL
records.title: Professional Work Experience/Internship
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: By department permission; VIT ENOL 113; VIT ENOL 280.
records.description: Undergraduate professional experience or internship course designed to complement the academic program, provide practical learning, and facilitate the transition to industry; one credit per 45 hours of approved experience.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.
